title: How Meta designed Muse: an AI agent people actually want to talk to | Alex Cornell (Design Director)
text: How Meta designed Muse: an AI agent people actually want to talk to | Alex Cornell (Design Director) Subscribe Sign in Playback speed × Share post Share post at current time Share from 0:00 0:00 / 6 How Meta designed Muse: an AI agent people actually want to talk to | Alex Cornell (Design Director) 🎙️ Alex Cornell explains how Muse serves your mom and an engineer with the same interface, and demos a SkyMall-style catalog, golf recaps, and a blog turned podcast Claire Vo Oct 12, 2026 6 Share Transcript Alex Cornell is a design director at Meta, where he leads design on Muse, Meta’s consumer AI agent. He came to the role with a long background in software product design, including time as a founder, and has spent the past year building one of the most thoughtful agent interfaces in the consumer AI space. Muse ships with a custom avatar, a three-layer status display, a personalized ideas surface, and a generative feed. Alex has been sharing the reasoning behind each of those design decisions publicly on Threads. Listen or watch on YouTube , Spotify , or Apple Podcasts What you’ll learn: Why Alex built Muse to feel like messaging, not an AI app How Muse’s three-layer status system accommodates different levels of technical expertise What generative UI actually means in a shipped consumer product How Alex turned years of forgotten Instagram saves into a daily shopping catalog Why his mom apologized to her Muse, and what it means for AI design How he uses Muse to track his golf game, shot by shot, as he works toward a single-digit handicap The mindset shift designers need when the output is never pixel-perfect When to use the main chat versus a side chat, and where the architecture still falls short Brought to you by: WorkOS —Make your app enterprise-ready, with SSO, SCIM, RBAC, and more In
